name: Sheepshead
description: Sheepshead is a trick-taking game derived from Schafkopf and widely played in Wisconsin and other German-American communities. Standard play uses five players, a 32-card piquet deck, a two-card blind, and a hidden partner mechanic where the picker and partner try to reach 61 card points.

content.text: Sheepshead is a trick-taking game derived from Schafkopf and widely played in Wisconsin and other German-American communities. Standard play uses five players, a 32-card piquet deck, a two-card blind, and a hidden partner mechanic where the picker and partner try to reach 61 card points.
Sheepshead is the American descendant of Schafkopf, brought by German immigrants and adapted into regional U.S. rulesets.
Standard game is five players with changing teams each hand; variants exist for 2-8 players.
Use a 32-card piquet deck (remove 2-6 from each suit in a standard deck).
Cards and score tracking for game points.
In the common five-player form, deal 6 cards to each player and 2 cards face down to the blind.

items.text: Called Ace: Picker calls an ace in a fail suit; holder becomes hidden partner until revealed by play.
Jack of Diamonds: Player holding jack of diamonds is partner; partnership remains hidden longer in many tables.
